role: Analytics Engineer I - AI & Data Enablement

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Write clean, production-grade SQL transformations using industry best practices for version control, testing, and data quality.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities emphasize testing, data quality, validation, and responsible practices throughout with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: You can contribute to simple data transformations and documentation with guidance.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Delivery/marketplace platform generates business-decision-affecting data but no explicit financial reporting, regulatory, or compliance language appears in the responsibilities.
evidence.collaboration_width: Data Analysts; Product Managers; Business stakeholders; other Data teams
evidence.data_team_maturity: As part of DataX, you will help us make data more accessible, reliable and useful for business teams
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A named data organization (DataX) with an established AI & Data Enablement team, senior engineers to mentor juniors, and existing global data models indicates a mature, established data function despite this being an entry-level hire.
evidence.jd_authorship: Write clean, production-grade SQL transformations using industry best practices for version control, testing, and data quality.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Specific technical detail (facts, dimensions, granularity, BigQuery, dbt, Looker, version control) alongside a clear entry-level growth path makes the day-to-day work concrete.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You will work closely with Data Analysts, Product Managers, Business stakeholders and other Data teams to understand problems, build trusted data assets
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the internal data function itself (DataX, other Data teams, data assets accessible to business teams) even though Product Managers are also named.
evidence.autonomy_level: Work side-by-side with senior engineers in a supportive environment designed to help you rapidly evolve into an autonomous Analytics Engineer.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Explicitly an entry-level, guided role ('contribute... with guidance', 'work side-by-side with senior engineers') with autonomy framed as a future growth trajectory rather than current scope.
evidence.ai_role: we are looking for someone who is already AI-savvy and has practical experience using AI tools to improve their work
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to use AI/GenAI tools to accelerate their own coding and analysis work, with AI framed explicitly as the candidate's productivity tool.
evidence.testing_framing: Write clean, production-grade SQL transformations using industry best practices for version control, testing, and data quality.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data quality are named as an owned responsibility within core SQL/engineering practice rather than only appearing in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: You can validate outputs and raise quality concerns when something does not look right.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: emphasis is on data reliability, validation, and responsible AI use rather than explicit regulatory or compliance risk language.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build High-Impact Data Models: Design reliable datasets and data models that power critical business decisions across global teams.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities mix building new data models/products with contributing to existing team workflows and data assets, with no dominant signal either way.
evidence.language_gate: Collaborator & Communicator: High attention to detail, clear communication skills across technical and non-technical teams, and fluent English.
evidence.work_arrangement: the freedom to work from home two days a week, and the opportunity to work from anywhere for up to three weeks a year
